Useful second derivatives look feasible, but the current implementation deliberately stops at first order. The main obstacle is that frameworks receive opaque Rust pullbacks, so they cannot differentiate those pullbacks again. I’m checking how much of the numerical core could support that extension without a rewrite.

The numerical core has useful foundations: Bessel kernels already compute some second derivatives, and linear solves have analytic adjoints that reuse their factorization. The larger effort is carrying second derivatives through complete scattering workflows and validating lattice sums, resonances, and eigenmodes. I’d start with Hessian–vector products on one supported workflow.
